findings.chapter: Chapter 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: The one owned-fleet figure to quote: (c) ~$0.0033 per request (≈$3.33 per 1K) — owned fleet, hour-matched active-hours basis, 6-host average at the ~10 rps average.
findings.issue: The prose calls ~$0.0033/request (≈$3.33/1K) 'the one owned-fleet figure to quote', but the same chapter later quotes ~$49.13/1K for the 21-host peak fleet and ~$0.0029/request for the 21-host full-utilization peak. The text does qualify the latter as 'a traffic-level variant, not a new basis', so this is not a numerical contradiction; however, the phrase 'the one owned-fleet figure to quote' is ambiguous because it can be read as excluding the peak-fleet figure from all owned-fleet quoting. Clarify that the 6-host average is the default owned-fleet unit cost, while peak-fleet costs are separate capacity-provisioning figures.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace 'The one owned-fleet figure to quote' with 'The default owned-fleet unit-cost figure to quote (average traffic, hour-matched basis)' and explicitly state that peak-fleet figures are separate provisioning costs, not alternative unit costs.

findings.evidence: PDF p.111 (printed p.87): "on the wall-clock paid-occupancy basis ($87,600/mo — the same fleet paid for all 730 h/mo — ÷ the same month's ~57.4B input tokens, an active-hours (173.33 h) volume) the same volume gives ~655K input tokens per $1 — wall-clock spend over active-hours tokens, an hour-basis mismatch and not a 730-hour token rate."
findings.issue: The operation as written is inverted relative to the stated result. $87,600 ÷ 57.4B = 1.53×10⁻⁶ tokens per dollar, not ~655K; the stated figure requires 57.4B ÷ $87,600 = 655,251 tokens per dollar. Elsewhere in the book the same style is used correctly in the opposite direction ("$87,600 ÷ 6,240K ≈ $14.04", spend ÷ volume = cost), so the reader has to reverse the expression himself to reconcile it. Since this bullet is the source of the ~655K figure carried into Table 4-1's economic row and the sidebar table's qualifier, the printed arithmetic should be unambiguous.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the clause as "the same month's ~57.4B input tokens ÷ $87,600 gives ~655K input tokens per $1", keeping the operation and the result in the same direction as the surrounding ~2.76M derivation (which is written tokens/s ÷ $/s).

findings.chapter: Ch. 4 (The Anatomy of an AI Workload) — Note † (Table 4-1 economic row)
findings.evidence: Note † (PDF p.99, printed p.75) states verbatim: "The 730-hour volume at the same 92,000 tok/s offered rate would be ~241.8B (92,000 × 3,600 × 730), so the two figures differ only in which hour count is used for the spend (730 h paid vs 173.33 h active), while the token volume is the same active-hours volume in both". The preceding sentence had fixed the token volume at "~57.4B input tokens (6.24M requests × 9,200 = 57.4B)".
findings.issue: Non-sequitur / contradictory referent: the sentence first introduces a hypothetical 730-hour token volume (241.8B), then concludes with "so" that the token volume "is the same active-hours volume in both" (57.4B). The 241.8B figure is never used by the conclusion, and a naive read yields two different token volumes inside one argument. (The arithmetic itself checks: 92,000 × 3,600 × 730 = 241.78B; 57.4B/20,800 = 2.76M; 57.4B/87,600 = 655K.)
findings.fix_instruction: Split into two sentences: (1) state that ~2.76M and ~655K divide the same 57.4B active-hours token volume by two different spend bases ($20,800 vs $87,600), differing only by the 730/173.33 = 4.21 hour-count ratio; (2) add the 241.8B figure as a separate caution, e.g. "a true 730-hour token rate would divide by ~241.8B (92,000 × 3,600 × 730), not 57.4B — do not read 655K as a 730-hour token rate."
